briefings.title: Closing Plenary

people.name: Sebastian Buckup
people.role: Member of the Managing Board, World Economic Forum

people.name: Ohood Bint Khalfan Al Roumi
people.role: Minister of State for Government Development and the Future, United Arab Emirates

briefings.tldr: The inaugural Annual Meeting of Global Future Leaders concluded in Dubai with over 500 leaders committing to intergenerational collaboration, strategic foresight, and action-driven frameworks to navigate AI, climate, and economic shifts.

briefings.title: Reading the Youth Pulse
briefings.tldr: Global youth are experiencing a high-tech, highly interconnected reality that established leaders consistently underestimate, leading to severe entry-level job shortages, systemic education-to-work mismatches, and a growing demand for distributed, partnership-driven decision-making over tokenistic consultation.

briefings.title: Betazone: The Human-Machine Line
briefings.tldr: Robotics and physical AI are rapidly commercializing, shifting the core interface from traditional screens to personality, connection, and distributed environmental intelligence.

briefings.title: Opening Plenary
briefings.tldr: Global leaders and next-generation innovators at the World Economic Forum opening plenary in Dubai emphasized that while the world faces unprecedented geopolitical uncertainty, technological shifts, and climate disruption, young people retain immense optimism and agency to co-author a resilient future.

briefings.title: Trust Test for Agentic AI

people.name: Omar Sultan Al Olama
people.role: Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence, UAE

briefings.tldr: As agentic AI shifts from answering questions to executing autonomous decisions, a lack of mature governance and global consensus poses severe risks to human livelihood, safety, and trust.

briefings.title: World Economic Forum’s Chief Economists Outlook: September 2026

people.name: Ufuk Akcigit
people.role: Deputy Chief Economist and Director of Private Markets, World Bank Group

briefings.tldr: Despite ongoing disruptions from geopolitical conflicts, fragile energy markets, and lingering inflation, chief economists show a significant rebound in sentiment, with 56% expecting global economic conditions to remain stable or improve.

briefings.title: World Economic Forum Global Gender Gap Report Media Briefing 2026

people.name: Sue Duke
people.role: Managing Director for EMEA & LATAM, LinkedIn

people.name: Yann Zopf
people.role: Head of Media, World Economic Forum

briefings.tldr: The World Economic Forum’s Global Gender Gap Report 2026 shows the overall global gender gap index at 69.2%, meaning it will take 120 years at the current rate of change to reach full parity, with leadership parity stretched out to 90 years.

briefings.title: AI's real impact on jobs - what it means for you, your company and future generations
briefings.tldr: Artificial intelligence has created a foresight "fog" for modern business, accelerating job task changes to 9% annually by 2026 and requiring that workforce reskilling be treated as part of the core infrastructure stack rather than an afterthought.

briefings.title: The Hormuz shock, AI and China: the state of global energy, with Jason Bordoff

people.name: Jason Bordoff
people.role: Director, Center on Global Energy Policy

people.name: Roberto Booca
people.role: Head of the Centre for Energy and Materials, World Economic Forum

briefings.tldr: Despite the Strait of Hormuz closure being the largest oil supply disruption in history, global energy markets showed unexpected resilience due to shifting Chinese demand and high inventories; however, the transition to clean energy now faces critical "headwinds" caused by geopolitical fragmentation and the difficulty of de-risking dependence on Chinese supply chains.

briefings.title: Opening Plenary

people.name: Klaus Schwab
people.role: Founder and Executive Chairman, World Economic Forum

people.name: Li Qiang
people.role: Premier of the People's Republic of China

briefings.tldr: The 17th Annual Meeting of the New Champions ("Summer Davos") in Dalian, China, convened over 1,800 global leaders to focus on the theme of "Innovating at Scale."

briefings.title: The Latest on Industrial Clusters

people.name: Jörgen Sandström
people.role: Head of Energy, Materials and Infrastructure Programs, World Economic Forum

briefings.tldr: Industrial clusters serve as critical, co-located ecosystems for accelerating green and digital transitions through cross-industry collaboration and systemic planning.

briefings.title: Nature Is Infrastructure

people.name: Razan Al Mubarak
people.role: President, International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)
people.organization: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)

organizations: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)
briefings.tldr: Integrating natural capital into economic strategy is a core driver of long-term business competitiveness, profitability, and talent attraction.

briefings.title: The Next Billion Jobs

people.name: Faisal Alibrahim
people.role: Minister of Economy and Planning of Saudi Arabia

briefings.tldr: While the World Bank projects a 400 million youth job shortfall globally, the rapid expansion of AI and digital platforms offers an unprecedented engine for productivity and employment, provided governments, businesses, and educational institutions aggressively coordinate to prioritize entrepreneurship, continuous reskilling, and human-centric industrial policies.

briefings.title: The scientific advances ready to change the world: the Top 10 Emerging Technologies 2026

people.name: Kimmy Bettinger
people.role: Lead, Expert and Knowledge Communities, World Economic Forum

briefings.tldr: The World Economic Forum’s 14th annual Top 10 Emerging Technologies report highlights a paradigm shift toward hyper-personalized healthcare, highly localized production, and AI-driven scientific discovery capable of solving humanity's most pressing infrastructure, environmental, and medical challenges within the next five years.

briefings.title: Top 10 Emerging Technologies 2026

people.name: Mariette DiChristina
people.role: Dean, College of Communication, Boston University

briefings.tldr: The World Economic Forum’s launch of the Top 10 Emerging Technologies of 2026 report highlights breakthrough innovations—including quantum simulation, PFAS destruction, and AI world models—that are redefining scientific possibilities, decoupling resource capabilities from geographic constraints, and demanding agile, non-siloed regulatory frameworks to scale responsibly.

briefings.title: What Next for the Middle East?

people.name: Faisal Alibrahim
people.role: Minister of Economy and Planning of Saudi Arabia

people.name: Sigrid Kaag
people.role: Senior Humanitarian and Reconstruction Coordinator for Gaza, United Nations

briefings.tldr: Following a highly disruptive regional war in early 2026, the Middle East is navigating a fragile diplomatic off-ramp while rapidly accelerating domestic infrastructure, logistics, and renewable energy projects to build long-term economic resilience.

briefings.title: AMNC26 - What to expect from "Summer Davos"
briefings.tldr: The 17th Annual Meeting of the New Champions (Summer Davos 2026) in Dalian, China, brings together over 1,700 global leaders to focus on scaling technological innovation amidst a highly contested geopolitical landscape, while energy experts debate whether recent geopolitical shocks will ultimately accelerate or hinder the global transition to green energy.

briefings.title: Financial fragmentation: the $6 trillion cost of breaking the "plumbing" of global finance

people.name: Matt Strahan
people.role: Private Market Initiatives Lead, World Economic Forum

people.name: Daniel Tannebaum
people.role: Global Anti-Financial Crime Practice Leader, Oliver Wyman

people.name: Anne Walsh
people.role: Managing Partner and Chief Investment Officer, Guggenheim Partners

briefings.tldr: Growing geopolitical tensions and the weaponization of global finance are driving severe financial fragmentation.

briefings.title: Welcome to Cold War Two: historian Niall Ferguson on geopolitics in 2026
briefings.tldr: Historian Niall Ferguson argues that while we have entered "Cold War Two"—a period defined by US-China rivalry and AI-driven risks—the current era is significantly less dangerous than the mid-20th century, offering unprecedented opportunities for individual empowerment through technology.

briefings.title: The questions top Davos leaders are asking to start 2026
briefings.tldr: As the global order shifts toward a permanent state of multipolar uncertainty, leaders in 2026 must abandon nostalgia for past stability in favor of "thinking the unthinkable," prioritizing structural independence, and distinguishing between mere organizational momentum and meaningful impact.
